page.layout: One printed page: running head centred above the text; a page number at top left; a large engraved emblem (woodcut illustration) in the centre; a four-line verse epigram below the picture; a catchword-like word at the lower right.

l.i: Hispida latrantem laedit dum forte catellum
Bellua, sit stricti iuris imago tibi:
Nam rigoris nimius, strictum qui persequitur ius:

page.notes: The copperplate emblem shows a hand holding a balance with a crown above, a man with a quill and a dog attacking a smaller dog at right. The last word of the verse line 4 is partly worn ("secut" may be "secat"); "Summum" at lower right is a printed catchword in italic bold, read as given. The running head "EMBLEMA" is in small capitals with a bar over the final A. The heading is in Greek capitals, transcribed as printed.
